diagnostic_evidence.quote: This architecture substantially mitigates numerical variance, resulting in enhanced training stability and superior generalization performance.
the two algorithms exhibit comparable accuracy and stability, with no single method displaying a decisive advantage in these low-dimensional regimes
Regarding stability, the standard deviations reported for both methods are generally comparable in magnitude across the tested dimensions.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts consistent outperformance and substantial variance reduction. In Tables tex2d1, tex2d2 and tex2d8, DBDP1 has smaller relative errors and smaller standard deviations in several settings (e.g. d=8: 2.9% vs 6.9%). DBR's standard deviations are often larger (tex1 at d=200; tex2d20). The body itself concedes that the methods are comparable and that variances are comparable.

failure_location.quote: Numerical results demonstrate that the DBR scheme consistently outperforms the DBDP1 method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claims to the settings where the data support them (Example 1 and the d=15 case), and drop the general variance-reduction claim or substantiate it.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised empirical advantage and variance-reduction mechanism are not supported uniformly by the reported data.
issues.title: Abstract claims consistent superiority and variance reduction contradicted by the paper's own tables
issues.why_classification: A headline claim about what the paper demonstrates must be withdrawn or narrowed, which is a material loss in advertised scope; no mathematics needs repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The 'relative error' is computed from the mean of 10 runs. At d=20 (u=0.259), DBR's standard deviation (0.446) and mean absolute error (0.366) exceed |u|, so individual runs err by more than 100%. At N=90 and N=100, DBDP1's mean absolute error is smaller than DBR's (0.265 vs 0.366; 0.235 vs 0.306). The claims of robustness and of DBDP1 'breakdown' versus DBR are therefore not supported.

failure_location.quote: the DBR scheme remains robust up to

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Report per-run error metrics and retract or qualify the robustness and superiority claims for d=15 and d=20.
issues.overall_effect: The central high-dimensional advantage claimed in the abstract, introduction and Section 5 for d=15 and d=20 is unsupported by the paper's own per-run accuracy metric.
issues.title: Claimed d=20 robustness rests on the error of the 10-run mean while per-run errors exceed the solution and DBDP1's
issues.why_classification: A main advertised empirical conclusion must be withdrawn or substantially qualified. No theoretical content is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The Z-loss label is the K-sample average of Y_{i+1} ΔW/h. This depends directly on ΔW, and its variance is of order 1/(hK), which grows as h→0. The stated noise-smoothing mechanism is therefore misdescribed.

failure_location.quote: the loss function of regression-based methods does not directly depend on $\Delta W_i$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the statement: the Z-label depends on ΔW and its Monte Carlo variance scales like 1/(hK).
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the variance-reduction advantage is misleading for the Z-component.
issues.title: False claim that the DBR loss does not depend directly on Brownian increments
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of a heuristic claim. No theorem or guarantee depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop runs over i=N-1,...,0, yet computes X_{i+1}^{π,m} from X_i^{π,m}. At i=N-1, X_{N-1}^{π,m} has not been generated, so the forward simulation is ill-defined as written. The Y-loss also uses X_i^{π,m,k}, which is never defined: only X_{i+1}^{π,m,k} is generated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Simulate all forward paths before the backward loop, and evaluate Z and f at X_i^{π,m}.
issues.overall_effect: The pseudocode does not define an executable procedure without restructuring.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 simulates the forward path inside the backward loop and uses undefined states
issues.why_classification: The fix is local and evident from the scheme description. The method and its guarantees are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: S_{y,i} is built from network outputs NN_{y,i+1}(p^{m,k}_{i+1}), NN_{y,i} and NN_{z,i}. R^y_{i,2} is built from the true values Y^{π,m,k}_{i+1}, Y^{π,m}_i and Z^{π,m}_i. Hence E|Y_i−S_{y,i}|^2 ≠ E|R^y_{i,2}|^2 in general; the difference contains the propagated network errors. The same false identity is used for Z in (Deep-NN-E-9-1-z).

failure_location.quote: From (\ref{NS-DMC}) and the definition of $S_{y,i}\left(p_{i}^{m}, X_{i+1}^{\pi,m} \right)$, we have

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the network residuals relative to the network-built labels (as in Huré–Pham–Warin and Germain–Pham–Warin), then redo the stability recursion so that propagated network errors enter through the Gronwall term.
issues.overall_effect: The error bound of Theorem ae-DMCE is not established. The convergence theorem and the RDBR estimate, which reuse Step 2, are not established either.
issues.title: False identity equating the fitting error to the residual R_{i,2}
issues.why_classification: A contained redefinition plus a re-derived recursion yields a comparable error bound. No new global architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: E|S_{y,i}−U_i|^2 is bounded by C(1+h)+…, an O(1) term, because the K-average is replaced by a single path and the variance is bounded by E|NN|^2. This constant vanishes in (Deep-NN-E-10). Kept, it gives (1/h)Σ_i O(1)=O(N^2) in (Deep-NN-E-8). Likewise, the CN term from (Deep-NN-E-9-z-1), multiplied by 2h, is an O(1) per-step term that disappears in (Deep-NN-E-16-1); summed, it gives O(N).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the 1/K_i variance factor of the K-sample averages, giving per-step terms of order 1/K, and add the resulting N^2/K-type term to the bound. This is absorbed by the choice K=O(N^3) in thm:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: As derived, the bounds on both the Y and Z errors diverge as N grows. The stated estimate and the downstream half-order convergence are unproven.
issues.title: Non-vanishing Monte Carlo fluctuation terms silently dropped in Y and Z estimates
issues.why_classification: A contained variance argument and an extra term restore a comparable bound and rate. The statement changes only by an added Monte Carlo term.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem ae-DMCE bounds the error by E|R_{i,2}|^2, the residual of θ* minimizing an M-sample empirical loss, relative to true discrete values. The proof only bounds the infimum of the L^2 approximation error of the auxiliary functions y_i and z_i over the GroupSort class. It never shows that E|R_{i,2}|^2 is controlled by this infimum: optimization and generalization errors and the y_i-versus-Y^π mismatch are ignored.

failure_location.quote: it suffices to choose the parameters $R, \varepsilon,K$ such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the result under the assumption that the population loss is minimized exactly (or add optimization and generalization error terms), and relate R_{i,2} to the approximation infimum.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h) mean-square convergence (half-order rate) is not established for the trained scheme.
issues.title: Best-approximation bounds substituted for residuals of empirically trained networks
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the hypothesis gives a recognizably comparable convergence statement, as in Germain–Pham–Warin.

issues.failure_explanation: The RDBR labels (S_{y,i}, and U-bar in Deep-NN-E-R) use the unreflected network NN_{y,i+1}. The discrete RBSDE propagates the reflected value max{Y-bar, g}. The recursion bounds E|Y-bar_i − Ŷ_i|^2 (unreflected Y, reflected network) by E|Y_{i+1} − NN_{i+1}|^2 (reflected Y, unreflected network). These differ by O(1) where the obstacle is active, so Gronwall cannot close. Moreover, Ŷ_i − U-bar_i is not a network residual when g > NN.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must redefine the RDBR labels using the reflected values max{NN_{y,i+1}, g} and redo the error recursion, including the Z-estimate, for the reflected scheme.
issues.overall_effect: As specified, the RDBR scheme essentially approximates max{unreflected BSDE value, g} rather than the Snell-envelope solution. The variational-inequality error estimate is unsupported.
issues.title: RDBR recursion propagates unreflected network values; error recursion does not close
issues.why_classification: Both the scheme and the proof need new construction, and the claimed extension to variational inequalities is not established.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem bounds the combined Y and Z error by Cε(h), with ε(h)=O(h) under Assumption 2. The only input for the Z discretization error gives O(h^{1/2}) regardless of the assumption, so the Z part cannot be O(h).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the Z-part bound as O(h^{1/2}) (or supply a stronger Z discretization estimate), keeping ε(h) only for the Y-part.
issues.overall_effect: The improved rate under Assumption 2 is unsupported for the Z-component.
issues.title: Z-error claimed O(h) under Assumption 2 while the cited discretization Z-error is only O(h^{1/2})
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the stated rate for one component; the rest of the result is unaffected.
